domain: Monetary Theory / Technology Governance / Political Economy
topic_summary: Analysis of cryptocurrency as a contested kernel with three candidate readings: sound-money (inflation hedge, store of value), speculative-asset (price appreciation vehicle), and decentralization-ideology (censorship resistance, sovereignty). The core question is whether these are three readings of one shared commitment or three distinct kernels sharing a technological substrate.

key_entities: Speculative traders (retail and institutional capital seeking returns)
Central banks and monetary authorities (fiat currency issuers)
key_tensions: Fixed supply (sound-money reading) vs price volatility (speculative reading)
Decentralization commitment (ideology reading) vs institutional adoption (speculative reading)
Censorship resistance (ideology reading) vs regulatory compliance (all readings under state pressure)
key_mechanisms: Exchange-mediated price discovery (enables speculation, undermines self-custody)
Regulatory classification (commodity vs security vs currency determines legal constraint)
Network effect accumulation (winner-take-all dynamics vs fragmentation)
key_absences: Actual transaction usage data (payment vs speculation vs hoarding)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Cryptocurrency as a technological commitment to algorithmic scarcity and distributed consensus
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: No single interpretive authority; competing communities claim legitimacy via different groundings (economic theory, market performance, ideological purity)
commitment_system_recognition.collapse_analysis: Initial hypothesis: three readings of one kernel. Testing reveals THREE DISTINCT KERNELS sharing a technological substrate. Sound-money reading grounds commitment in scarcity (Austrian monetary theory). Speculative reading grounds commitment in price appreciation (market performance). Decentralization reading grounds commitment in censorship resistance (cypherpunk ideology). These are not different interpretations of one shared commitment—they are three separate commitments that happen to use the same technology. A sound-money advocate and a speculator do not disagree about what Bitcoin IS; they agree it is scarce digital tokens, but one values scarcity-as-inflation-hedge while the other values scarcity-as-supply-constraint-for-price-pumping. The substrate (blockchain, proof-of-work, fixed supply) is shared infrastructure, not a kernel. Coherence test fails: removing any reading does not change what the other readings constrain. This is three parallel constraint systems, not one contested kernel.

omegas.description: The three candidate readings (sound-money, speculation, decentralization) are not readings of one kernel but three distinct kernels sharing technological infrastructure. A sound-money advocate and a speculator agree on what Bitcoin is (scarce digital tokens) but value different properties. This is not interpretive disagreement about one commitment but three parallel commitments. The 'cryptocurrency kernel' is a category error—there is no single shared commitment being read differently.

Extraction identifies absence of actual transaction usage data. If cryptocurrency is primarily held for speculation rather than used for payments, the sound-money reading collapses into a speculative narrative with Austrian-economics branding. Observable: ratio of transaction volume to exchange volume.

Deferred axis regulatory_classification_uncertainty has high epsilon but unstable observable. If SEC classifies most tokens as securities, the decentralization reading becomes a piton (atrophied sovereignty claim). If classified as commodities, speculation reading gains institutional legitimacy. Classification is upstream to all three selected axes but too uncertain for generation.
omegas.source: Deferred axis with high epsilon + Dark Matter Probe 3

omegas.description: Energy_externality_mountain classified as low-epsilon mountain, but global carbon pricing or proof-of-stake transition could reclassify it as high-epsilon snare. If energy costs are internalized, proof-of-work becomes economically unviable, collapsing sound-money and decentralization readings that depend on it.

Deferred axis institutional_capture_drift suggests decentralization commitment may be a piton rather than tangled_rope. If exchange custody becomes dominant (already >80% of supply), censorship resistance becomes theoretical rather than operational. Observable: self-custody adoption trajectory.
